svg.title: Partial Adoption of Inquiry — Preferences and a Conditional Method
svg.desc: An agent's existing preferences and meta-preferences can support independent practical concerns as well as concerns motivating a conditional inquiry method, such as responsiveness to what is right or avoidance of reflective error. The agent considers both routes when choosing action. These routes overlap rather than partition preferences, do not impose a fixed allocation, and the method can sometimes converge on ordinary preference satisfaction.

g.text: The two routes are overlapping aspects of evaluation, not exclusive categories.
The agent decides whether, where, and how strongly to use the method.
Ends regardless of their benefit to inquiry
Respond to reasons; avoid missed chances
No universal duty to adopt the method
Consider independent ends and method-informed assessment
